name: Kourou ZLV (Vega launch complex)
tagline: Kourou's first launch site: Europa II, Ariane 1 and Giotto on this ground, rebuilt in 2001 for Vega and Vega-C
description: Three launch bases have stood on this spot at Kourou. Europe built the first for the Europa II, whose only flight on 5 November 1971 failed. Rebuilt as ELA-1, it flew Ariane 1 from 24 December 1979, then Ariane 2 and 3 until 11 July 1989. Giotto left from here on an Ariane 1 on 2 July 1985 to meet Halley's Comet. From November 2001 the pad was rebuilt for Vega, keeping the Ariane 1 flame trench and adding a 50 m retractable assembly building. Vega first flew on 13 February 2012, Vega-C on 13 July 2022. Payloads include LISA Pathfinder, Sentinel-2A and 2B, ADM-Aeolus and BIOMASS. Wikipedia counts 56 launches from the site by September 2026, 22 of them Vega and 8 Vega-C. The tower sits close to the equator at 5.2 degrees north.
